title: More specific wording narrowed semantic representations in four language models
summary: Researchers compared sentences that made a meaning more specific with sentences that merely added detail. Across four language models, the more specific versions formed tighter neighborhoods in model activation space. The pattern persisted after removing five dominant directions of variation.

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 abstract and affiliation, refinement design, Figure 5, permutation tests and quality-controlled rerun

evidence.tested: Controlled refinement and elaboration chains were checked using blind human judgments. Across the four models, the contraction contrast persisted in 86–100% of layers after the five dominant directions were removed.
evidence.unknown: The result depends on the constructed text contrasts and representation measures. It does not demonstrate causal use of the contraction in other language tasks.
evidence.ai_role: Pretrained activation geometry is measured as controlled texts move from broader meanings to more specific descriptions, with blind human checks on the contrasts.
